blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Geospatial text spotting involves locating and transcribing geographic labels, such as road names, district names, and landmarks, in raster maps. These labels are often small, densely arranged, and arbitrarily oriented. Although Arabic text recognition has been studied extensively in documents and natural scenes, Arabic geospatial text spotting remains underexplored. We introduce ARABGEOTEXT, an Arabic-centric benchmark covering 970 geographic locations in Riyadh and Jeddah, with 17,875 manually annotated text instances per view type. For each location, we pair an OpenStreetMap (OSM) rendering with a composite created by overlaying that rendering on the corresponding remote sensing (RS) imagery. The paired views preserve label content and pixel geometry, allowing evaluation across different backgrounds. Geographic partitions support in-city and city-disjoint evaluation of detection, recognition, and end-to-end spotting. Experiments with direct Qwen3.5-4B spotting show difficulties in recovering all labels within a tile. We therefore propose a tool-augmented vision-language framework that combines YOLO26 localization and crop rectification with Qwen3.5-4B recognition adapted through low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The framework outperforms direct LoRA-adapted Qwen3.5-4B spotting across both image views and test cities. With localization held fixed, reader adaptation further improves recognition over the pretrained zero-shot reader. The dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yakoubbazi/ArabGeoText.
blocks.zh: 地理空间文本的定位涉及在光栅图中定位和转录地理标签,如道路名称、区名和地标等。 这些标签往往很小、排列密集并任意取向。 尽管在文件和自然场景中广泛研究了阿拉伯文文本识别,但阿拉伯文地理空间文本的显示仍然没有得到充分利用。 我们采用阿拉伯GEOT,这是一个以阿拉伯为中心的基准,涵盖利雅得和吉达的970个地理位置,每个视图类型有17 875个手动附加说明的文字实例。 对于每个地点,我们把OpenStreetMap(OSM)的渲染与通过在相应的遥感图像上覆盖渲染而创建的复合材料配对。 配对的视图保留了标签内容和像素几何,允许不同背景的评价. 地理分区支持市内和市内对检测,识别,端对端抽查进行联合评价. 直接使用Quen3.5-4B分取的实验显示,在平板内回收所有标签有困难。 因此,我们提出一个工具强化的远景语言框架,将YOLO26本地化和作物整顿与通过低等级调整而适应的Quen3.5-4B识别结合起来(LORA)。 这个框架的效绩超过了直接经过LORA调整的Quen3.5-4B在图像视图和测试城市中所发现的. 随着本地化的固定进行,读者的适应性比预先训练的零镜头阅读器进一步提高了认知. 数据集和代码将在https://github.com/yakoubazi/ArabGeoText上公布。

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Geographic names identify roads, districts, and landmarks,
complementing the physical features visible in remote sensing
(RS) imagery. Extracting these names from raster maps and
map–imagery composites supports place-name search and geographic
image interpretation, and helps link map content to geographic
databases [ 1 ] . Geographic information systems can provide names as structured
records, but these records may be unavailable when only a rendered
image is available. In that case, names must be recovered directly
from pixels.
Geospatial text spotting addresses this task by locating
visible text instances and producing their transcriptions.

blocks.en:
We introduce ArabGeoText , an Arabic-centric benchmark
for geospatial text spotting covering 970 locations in
Riyadh and Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Each location provides
paired OpenStreetMap (OSM) renderings and RS imagery
overlaid with OSM (RS+OSM), preserving identical label

17,875 manually annotated text instances per view type,
with polygons and transcriptions for predominantly Arabic
text, together with Latin-script, mixed-script, and numeric
or symbolic labels naturally present in the maps.
The training, validation, and in-city test partitions are
drawn from Riyadh, while Jeddah is reserved for city-disjoint
testing.

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: II-A Map Text Spotting and Arabic Text Recognition
blocks.zh: II-A 地图文本示意图和阿拉伯文本识别

blocks.en: Map text extraction requires the localization and recognition of labels whose orientation, spacing, and placement are influenced by geographic features. Existing systems integrate text extraction and linking within pipelines for historical maps [ 1 ] , while dedicated competitions evaluate detection, recognition, and the linking of separate words into geographic names [ 2 , 3 ] . Hyper-local feature sampling and positional representations have also been used to detect and recognize long, rotated labels [ 18 ] . Complementary approaches address text linking by combining textual content, visual features, and polygon geometry [ 19 ] . These studies highlight the roles of local appearance and spatial relationships in map understanding. Their historical-map setting, however, differs from the contemporary digital maps and map–imagery composites considered here, where the same rendered labels can be examined against different backgrounds.
blocks.zh: 地图文本取出需要定位和识别其取向,间隔,和放置受地貌所影响的标签. 现有系统整合了历史地图的文本取出和管道内的连接[1],而专门的竞赛则评价检测,识别,以及将单独的单词连接到地名[2,3]. 超局部特征取样和位置表示也被用来检测和识别长而旋转的标签 [18]. 补充方法涉及将文字内容、视觉特征和多边形几何组合起来的文本链接[19]。 这些研究突出了局部外观和空间关系在地图理解中的作用. 然而,它们的历史地图设定不同于本文所考虑的当代数字地图和地图-图象复合材料,在这些地图中,可以根据不同的背景来检查相同的标签。

blocks.en: Arabic text recognition has been studied across handwritten and printed text [ 5 , 6 ] , as well as text in natural scenes [ 4 ] . More recent resources broaden the evaluation to document understanding [ 7 ] , synthetic book-style text [ 8 ] , and calligraphic text and multimodal understanding [ 9 ] . These resources cover diverse Arabic recognition settings, but do not examine geographic labels in paired map and map–imagery views. In our dataset, fixed label content and geometry allow background effects to be examined, while the city-based partitions support evaluation of geographic generalization.

blocks.en: II-B Vision–Language Models for Text and Geospatial Understanding
blocks.zh: II-B 愿景-文本和地理空间理解语言模型

blocks.en:
Vision–language approaches to text processing combine
recognition, localization, and reasoning in different ways. Encoder–decoder
models formulate text recognition as sequence generation using
pretrained visual and language representations [ 13 ] .
More recent approaches unify optical character recognition across
scene and document images, supporting whole-page processing and
region-level recognition guided by coordinates or visual
cues [ 14 ] . Compact vision–language models also incorporate
text spotting alongside document parsing [ 20 ] .
Evaluation spans diverse text-processing tasks [ 21 ] , as
well as visual document grounding and referring [ 22 ] .
The requirements differ across these settings. Recognition
from a supplied crop focuses on transcription, whereas full-image
spotting also requires localization and the association of each
transcription with its spatial extent. Tool-assisted
approaches obtain fine-grained evidence by invoking expert
agents to ground multimodal reasoning in visual and textual
elements [ 23 ] .

blocks.en:
In RS, vision–language models have been developed
for image captioning and question answering [ 10 ] ,
as well as multisensor interpretation [ 11 ] .
Geographic data also provide supervision for
constructing image–language training
data [ 24 ] , training foundation models with structured
map information [ 25 ] , and aligning image-patch
representations with geographic semantics [ 26 ] .
Other work uses paired aerial images and rendered maps to
generate geographically informed captions for domain
adaptation [ 27 ] . These approaches primarily use
geographic information to support image interpretation.
Related visual-grounding methods address spatial localization
through adaptive modality guidance [ 28 ] , unified prediction
of horizontal boxes, oriented boxes, and masks [ 29 ] ,
or progressive visual search in large scenes [ 30 ] .
These methods locate objects specified by referring
expressions, whereas text spotting detects and transcribes
the text visible in an image.
Our work addresses Arabic text spotting in geospatial images
by combining text-region localization with vision–language
recognition. We compare this approach with direct prediction
of text regions and transcriptions from the full image.

the corresponding satellite image with a map opacity of 0.63 0.63 . This value keeps geographic labels visible while
retaining details of the underlying RS image. Both views
are used for text spotting.

individual text regions. It operates on the same OSM
or RS+OSM tiles as the direct VLM and predicts text
regions without producing transcriptions. The predicted masks define each text region for polygon
localization and crop preparation. The VLM then reads
the resulting crops.

blocks.en: VI Conclusion
blocks.zh: 六. 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced ArabGeoText , a benchmark for Arabic
geospatial text spotting in Riyadh and Jeddah. Each location
provides an OSM rendering and a composite formed by overlaying
the rendering on satellite imagery. The paired images preserve
the same labels and their pixel locations, allowing comparison
between the two views. The benchmark supports evaluation
within the training city and in an unseen city.

blocks.en:
We proposed a tool-augmented framework that combines YOLO26
text localization and crop rectification with LoRA-adapted
VLM recognition. The framework outperforms direct full-image
VLM spotting on both views and test cities. Reader adaptation
further improves recognition and end-to-end spotting.
Removing transcription from direct VLM generation improves
detection, but a substantial gap to YOLO26 remains.
These results support the use of specialized localization
followed by VLM recognition for this task.

这些成果支持使用专门的本地化

the benchmark to additional cities would allow a broader
evaluation of geographic generalization.
